title: Adjust Bending-Weft/Warp
content: ### **Objective** Use **Bending** intensity which is the resistant against being bent, to adjust the stiffness of fabric. The higher the value, the stiffer it becomes such as denim and leather, and the lower the value, the more it becomes suitable for draping materials such as silk. The Bending intensity for the weft and warp directions can be set separately likewise the real fabrics. **Location** Object Browser ▶ Fabric Property Editor ▶ Physical Property ▶ Detail ▶ **Bending-Weft** /**Warp** **Expressing materials with Weft (Horizontal) bending intensity** ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005548248/________01.png) **Expressing materials with Warp (Vertical) bending intensity** ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005548268/________02.png) **※Note:** Adjust Bending for bias by using **Bending - Bias** (ver.5.1.0).
content_description: Discover how to customize fabric stiffness by adjusting bending intensity in both weft and warp directions for optimal material performance.

title: Open Textures in AI / PS (ver 6.1)
content: ### **Objective** Open the texture image applied to fabric or trim in Adobe Illustrator/Photoshop. ### **Location** Fabric Property ▶ ![mceclip0.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/900008317346/mceclip0.png) button right to each map. ### **Operation** 1. Click the tool/menu indicated. → The pop-up menu appears. 2. Click Add Another App menu. → Select Application window appears. 3. Select the executable file (EXE) of the application to be added. Click Open button. → The texture will then open in that application and the application will be added to the list of the pop-up menu as well. 4. Save the edited texture in the application, return to CLO, then right-click on the background in the 3D window. ▶ Click **Refresh Textures (F5)**. → The edited texture image appears. **※Note:** * Once you click Open with Another App menu, you can only execute the selected application without adding it to the pop-up menu. * User Settings ▶ [Other](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/ko/articles/360001547188-%EA%B8%B0%ED%83%80-%EC%84%A4%EC%A0%95) you can register or delete the application that is opening textures.
content_description: This webpage provides a step-by-step guide for opening and editing texture images applied to fabric or trim in Adobe Illustrator/Photoshop through CLO, enhancing your design workflow.

Rendering thickness from the center of the Garment is set for 0.5mm as default vale, and it is adjustable. This thickness value is only visible and does not Simulate as the thickness value space out between Fabrics. **※ Note: **To see the rendering thickness, 3D Garment Rendering Style must be set on **Thick Textured Surface** . **Location** **Fabric Unit ** Object Browser ▶ Fabric ▶ Fabric Item ▶Property Editor ▶ **Thickness** **Pattern Unit**(ver2.3.0) Select Pattern in 2D/3D Window ▶ Property Editor ▶ Simulation Properties ▶ **Add'l Thickness-Rendering** **Operation** **Fabric Unit** 1. title: Adjust Buckling Ratio
content: **Objective** Use this function to reflect the tendency of Fabric trying to preserve its shape then being bent when applying certain amount of force. The closer the Buckling Ratio gets to 100 percent (%), the more it becomes easily bendable fabric such as silk and jersey. On the other hand, the closer the ration gets to 0 percent (%), the more it becomes less bendable fabric such as denim and wool. **Location** Object Browser ▶ Fabric Property Editor ▶ Physical Property ▶ Detail ▶ **Buckling Ratio** ![_____________.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115018758847/_____________.png) **※Note:** Adjust Buckling Ratio for bias by using **Buckling Ratio - Bias** (ver.5.1.0).
content_description: Explore how the Buckling Ratio influences fabric flexibility, showcasing the transition from bendable materials like silk to more rigid fabrics like denim.

title: Adjust Buckling Stiffness
content: **Objective** Adjust how much percentage (%) of total Bending intensity to use to decide the Buckling Stiffness of the corners of Fabric. This is used alongside Bending-Weft/Warp. For instance, entering a Buckling Stiffness of 80 when Bending value is 60, is going to result in the Bending value of the actual intensity of the part of the Fabric being folded being 80% of 60 which is 48. In other words, the higher the Buckling ratio, the harder it is to fold the corners of fabric, and on the other hand, the lower the the ratio, the easier it folds. **Location** Object Browser ▶ Fabric Property Editor ▶ Physical Property ▶ Detail ▶ **Buckling Stiffness-Weft** /**Warp** ** ** ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115005756128/____.png) **※Note:** Adjust Buckling Stiffness for bias by using **Buckling Stiffness - Bias** (ver.5.1.0).
content_description: This web page provides guidance on adjusting the percentage of total bending intensity to determine the buckling stiffness of fabric corners, influencing their foldability based on specified bending and buckling values.

Press **Compute** once finish putting the value and wait until automatic calculation for the fabric property is completed. 4. Save the calculated fabric as .zfab file. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/article_attachments/115000708348/1.PNG)
content_description: This webpage provides a step-by-step guide for digitizing new fabric properties and saving them as a .zfab file using the Emulator Mode in the application.

title: Unified Map 6.1
content: **Objective** When a pattern construction constrains a print layout, apply the texture using Unified Map. YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eqeB6edmo5A **Location** Object Browser ▶ Fabric Tab ▶ On the right button of Fabric Item **Texture Repeat / Unified Map**. Object Browser ▶ Fabric Tab ▶ Fabric Property Editor ▶ Material ▶**Texture Mapping** **Operation** 1. Click the tool/ menu indicated. 2. Use Unified Map to apply the texture differently. 3. Set the specific options of the Unified Map. Repeat U | Set the range for the image to be arranged between 0-1 in the U direction. ---|--- Repeat V | Set the range for the image to be arranged between 0-1 in the V direction. **※Note:** Once you have applied the Unified Fabric Map, the Edit Texture Tool will only rotate the Grain-line, NOT the Texture.

title: Import AxF file
content: ### Objective Express textures by using the AxF file of X-Rite that express realistic fabric materials with various maps extracted by three-dimensional scanning of fabric. **Location** Object Browser ▶ **Fabric** **Operation** 1. Click the tool/ menu indicated in Location. ** ** 2. Right click the fabric item and **Import/ Import (Add).** → **Open File** window appears. 3. Select the AxF file and click **Open**. → Fabric property is converted into the property of AxF file. → When using **Import (Add)** , the properties that have already set are retained, only the properties that are not present are changed to the corresponding Axf file. (Ex: When having texture only, the other maps are applied such as Normal, Alpha, or etc) **※ Note:** You can drag and drop the AxF file to **Fabric** in **Object Browser** , 2D Pattern, and 3D Garment.
content_description: Discover how to seamlessly import and apply realistic fabric textures using X-Rite's AxF files, enhancing your 3D designs with accurate material properties.

title: Specular Color
content: **List of Contents** Specular Color Apply Specular Color Adjust Shininess **Specular Color ** \- The **Specular Color** is the color of the light directly reflected from the fabric used to express glossy materials such as enamel. ** Apply Specular Color** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cYcwPAlf7SA \- Select the fabric item from the Object Browser. \- Navigate to the Property Editor and select the color chip next to the Material ▶**Specular Color.** \- When the color window appears, select the desired Specular Color. \- Brighter the Specular Color is, glossier the fabric will become. **Adjust Shininess** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6fxPbAKlpRc \- Select the fabric item from the Object Browser. \- Navigate to the Property Editor and expand the Material ▶ **Specular Color** to see its child menus. Locate the **Shininess** option. \- Move the scroll bar to adjust the gloss of the fabric. Higher the Shininess value is, glossier the fabric will become, like enamel. However, on the contrast, lower the Shininess value is, more regularly the gloss will spread on the surface of the fabric, like lame. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This webpage provides a comprehensive guide on applying and adjusting specular color and shininess for fabrics to achieve desired glossy effects.

title: Adjust Internal Damping
content: ### **Objective** Use this function to set resistance against the bouncing speed of Garments. Increasing the Internal Damping value is going to cause the Garment to slow down as if it is in underwater, and lowering the value is going to cause it to bounce very quickly. **※ Note:** Adjusting the measurement while putting Garments on does not make a noticeable difference therefore it is better to use during animation as it influences Garments when they are moving. **Location** Object Browser ▶ Fabric Property Editor ▶ Physical Property ▶ Detail ▶ **Internal Damping**
content_description: This web page provides guidance on adjusting the Internal Damping value to control the bouncing speed of garments during animation, enhancing realism in movement.

title: glTF a Standard Fabric File Compatibility (ver 6.1)

title: How long will it take me to learn CLO?
content: **Question** How long will it take me to learn CLO? **Answer** The learning pace for CLO software differs for each individual and depends on the hours of practice and the complexity of your project. Therefore, it is hard to estimate the learning period, but everyone can reach a professional level after a certain practice. Some CLO users get it quickly through online tutorials on various channels and communicating with other CLO users via [CLO community forum](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/community/topics). If you could build your network, you may be able to acquire more extensive knowledge than others. For more information, please refer to the article about the [Available Training Resources](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115013367088).
content_description: Discover how individual practice, project complexity, and community engagement influence your learning journey with CLO software.

title: Buttons: Change Thread Type and Material
content: **List of Contents** Change Thread Type and Material Change Thread Type for Buttons Change Material for Buttons **Change Thread Type and Material** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=E5SIXdPCctw \- Change thread type, material and color for the button thread. \- Object Browser ▶ Button Tab ▶ Property Editor ** Change Thread Type for Buttons** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gEod9kxh7iM \- Select the desired thread type. ** Change Material for Buttons** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2RYOVqdmOjE \- Choose the desired material for the button thread by navigating to Property Editor ▶ Material ▶ Thread tab. \- Turn off **Use Same Material as Button** option to apply different material to the button thread.
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide with video tutorials on how to change the thread type and material for buttons in your design projects.

title: [Mac] Open an App from Unidentified Developer
content: **Objective** Resolve issue when **Open an App from Unidentified Developer** message appears while installing or updating CLO in Mac. **Operation** 1. When installing or updating CLO in Mac, **Open an App from Unidentified Developer** message may appear as below. ![unidentified_app_2.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115009628508/unidentified_app_2.png) 2. Open **Security & Privacy** window. 3. Choose **Anywhere** under **Allow apps downloaded from**. **※Note** : If **Anywhere** option does not exist, select **Mac App Store and identified developers**. ![macOS-gatekeeper_2.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115009520427/macOS-gatekeeper_2.png) 4. Save the changes. → CLO will install or update properly. 5. Reference:[ Apple Manual](https://support.apple.com/kb/PH25088?locale=ko_KR&viewlocale=en_US) if needed.
content_description: This webpage provides a step-by-step guide to resolving the "Open an App from Unidentified Developer" message when installing or updating CLO on a Mac.

title: Create/Edit V-Ray Lights (ver 5.2)
content: # **List of Contents** Create Light Select/ Move/ Rotate Light Right-click Pop-up Menu **Objective** Create and edit various lights. YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RZw96hmGtiI **Location** **Create Light** Render Toolbar ▶ ![Render_Light.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360057252794/Render_Light.png) **Rectangle** /**Sphere** /**Spot** /**Directional** /**IES** / **Dome Light** ** Select Light ** Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶**Select/Move ** 3D Toolbar ▶**![Toolbar_3D_Select_Move.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115024215067/Toolbar_3D_Select_Move.png) Select/Move ** **Operation** **Create Light** 1. Select the tool indicated in Location. 2. Click a light to be created. → The light appears in the 3D Window. → The light's direction appears as a line. **Select/ Move/ Rotate Light** 1. Select the tool indicated in Location. 2. Click the light to select/ move/ rotate. → The light is selected and its [properties](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115014899168-V-Ray-%EB%A0%8C%EB%8D%94-%EC%A1%B0%EB%AA%85-%EC%86%8D%EC%84%B1-%EC%84%A4%EC%A0%95) appear in the Property Editor. → The Gizmo appears. 3. Use the [Gizmo](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000513928-%EA%B8%B0%EC%A6%88%EB%AA%A8%EB%A1%9C-%ED%8C%A8%ED%84%B4-%EC%9D%B4%EB%8F%99-%ED%9A%8C%EC%A0%84) to move or rotate the light. → The light is moved or rotated accordingly. **Right-click Pop-up Menu** 1. Select the tool indicated in Location. 2. Right-click on the light. → The right-click pop-up menu appears. 3. Click the menu below as needed. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- ** Select All Lights ** | Select all lights. **Delete/Deactivate Light/Hide Light** | Delete, deactivate, or hide the selected light. **Show All Lights** | Show all hidden lights in the 3D Window. **※ Note:** Show or hide lights by using the icon in the 3D Window. ![3D_Show.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360058091373/3D_Show.png) Environment Display ▶ ![Show_Light_Render.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360058091353/Show_Light_Render.png) **Show Light (Render)** Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to provide comprehensive instructions for creating and managing various light types within a 3D environment.

title: Copy/Save V-Ray Render Image
content: **List of Contents** Copy Save **Objective** Easily use the preview image in the Render window by copying and saving the preview. **※ Note:** The image appears in the Render window is a preview image, whereas the [final render image](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115014784747) is a high quality image which all render, light, and image/video properties are fully applied. **Location ** **Copy ** Render Toolbar ▶ ![copy_current_image.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115025911107/copy_current_image.png) **Copy Current Image** ** Save ** Render Toolbar ▶ ![save_current_image.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115025911127/save_current_image.png) **Save Current Image** ** Operation** **Copy** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Render Toolbar ▶ ![copy_current_image.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115025911107/copy_current_image.png) **Copy Current Image** → The preview image in the Render window is copied to the clipboard and can be pasted to other programs as needed. **Save** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Render Toolbar ▶ ![save_current_image.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115025911127/save_current_image.png) **Save Current Image** → The Save Image File window appears. 2. Name the image and designate the saving path. Then, select **Save**. → The image is saved. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a straightforward guide on how to copy and save the preview image from the Render window for easy use in other applications.
